newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal begins surveillance on flood fear.
newsitem.headline: Nepal begins surveillance on flood fear.

text.p: Nepali army and glacier experts have set up a surveillance post to monitor a glacial lake in central Nepal that might burst its banks, state radio said on Friday.
"The team (of experts) will carry out the research on the glacier throughout the rainy season," it said.

Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology last month warned that the size of the Tsho-Rolpa glacial lake in Rolwaling Valley, 140 kilometres (90 miles) northeast of Kathmandu, had increased to 1.65 sq km (0.64 sq mile) from 1.37 sq km in 1993.

The government ordered the evacuation of people living downstream from the lake following the department's warning that it could burst during the current monsoon season which continues through September.
Rituraj Bhandari, the seniormost civil servant of Dolakha district, where the lake is located, said siphons were being installed to drain out the lake to avoid possible disaster.
He said many people had already left their homes for safer places after the government warning.
"Special communication facilities have been installed and sirens will be fitted to warn the people in case the lake bursts," Bhandari told Reuters by phone from Dolakha.
Tsho-Rolpa lies in the Gaurishankar mountain range at an altitude of 4,580 metres (15,026 ft) and is close to the kingdom's border with China.
